Font Examples — 15 Fancy Google Fonts

Fifteen free display/script families picked from the fonts.google.com Feeling filters (Expressive: Fancy, Futuristic, Active, Awkward) and Calligraphy filter (Script: Formal). Each block renders in its own font: regular, bold, italic, bold-italic, underline, strikethrough and extra styles.

Fonts are not stored in this repository — install them on your machine and point the converter at them: CLI: gowkhtmltopdf --font-path font-examples.html out.pdf · Library: conv.Global().Set("fontpath", "") (both Converter and ImageConverter). On this dev machine the fonts are installed in a standard user font folder (~/.local/share/fonts), so --use-system-fonts also finds them.

Engine limits: static TrueType TTFs only (variable fonts and CFF/OTTO are rejected); most of these faces are single-weight, so bold is synthesized for Latin text and italic falls back to the regular face (no italic synthesis); overline is unsupported (underline/strikethrough are fine). Tangerine ships a real Bold face.

How to get these fonts: fonts.google.com → Feeling / Calligraphy filters, download each family, unzip, and pass the folder to --font-path (repeatable) or --use-system-fonts. In Go code: conv.Global().Set("fontpath", "/abs/path") on either Converter or ImageConverter. The engine embeds only the glyphs used (font subsetting), so output stays small.
